newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU 14 Sept mid distillate stocks fall 2.93 mln bls.
newsitem.headline: EU 14 Sept mid distillate stocks fall 2.93 mln bls.

text.p: Middle distillate stocks in the European Union, excluding Sweden, fell 2.93 million barrels, or 1.0 percent, in September to 283.35 million barrels, Stitchting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.

The draw leaves middle distillate stocks even further behind year ago levels. Year-on-year, the stocks are down 33.47 million barrels, or 10.6 percent, compared with 25.79 million barrels, or 8.3 percent, at the end of August.
Month-on-month, stocks fell by most in the Netherlands, down 2.63 million barrels. German stocks were stable.

Crude and oil product stocks fell by 8.04 million barrels, or 0.8 percent, in September to 1.002 million barrels. The inventories were also 4.2 percent, or 43.97 million barrels lower than at the end of September 1995.
Individually, stocks of crude and all products, except gasoline, were down.

Fuel oil inventories were down 2.21 million barrels, or 1.6 percent, to 138.58 million barrels. Despite the drop, the shortfall was not as acute as at the end of August. The year-on-year deficit was 11.75 million barrels, or 7.8 percent, against a year-on-year deficit of 15.83 million barrels, or 10.1 percent, at the end of August.

Crude stocks fell 6.13 million barrels, or 1.5 percent, to 398.22 million barrels at the end of September. Regionally, the greatest drops were respectively of 3.29 million and 3.28 barrels in France and the Netherlands.
Gasoline inventories were up 3.23 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, to 156.74 million barrels. France and Italy both registered the largest rises, each of 1.28 million barrels.
Naphtha stocks were steady at 24.64 million barrels.
Crude intake was 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) lower than in August at 11.098 million bpd, leading to a utilisation rate of 88.08 percent in September, against 88.41 percent in August.
